\section{Introduction}
Sediment transport in alluvial channels couples the shallow water
equations to the Exner equation for bed evolution. Numerical schemes
for this coupled system must handle the stiffness introduced when the
bed response time is much shorter than the flow time scale.

The governing equations in one dimension are
\begin{equation}
\partial_t h + \partial_x q = 0, \qquad
\partial_t q + \partial_x \left( \frac{q^2}{h} + \frac{g h^2}{2} \right)
= -g h \, \partial_x z_b - g h \, S_f,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
(1 - \phi) \, \partial_t z_b + \partial_x q_s = 0,
\end{equation}
where $\phi$ is the bed porosity, $q_s$ is the volumetric sediment flux,
and $S_f$ is the friction slope.

A standard closure writes $S_f = C_f \, q \, |q| / h^2$, which is
singular as $h \to 0$. Following recent practice we regularise the
closure with a small parameter $\varepsilon$ so that
\begin{equation}
S_f = C_f \, \frac{q \, |q|}{h^2 + \varepsilon^2},
\end{equation}
and we require convergence to the dry-bed limit as the parameter
vanishes.

\section{Numerical Scheme}
The hyperbolic part is discretised with a Godunov-type finite volume
scheme. The numerical flux at the interface between cells $i$ and
$i+1$ uses the Harten--Lax--van Leer approximation, and the bed slope
source term is upwinded following the hydrostatic reconstruction.

The friction term is treated implicitly. Writing the semi-discrete
update as $q^{n+1} = q^{*} - \Delta t \, g h^n S_f^{n+1}$ and
substituting the regularised closure gives a scalar nonlinear equation
for $q^{n+1}$, which we solve by Newton iteration.

The iteration is stopped when the residual falls below the tolerance
$\epsilon = 10^{-10}$. In all computations reported here the
regularisation parameter is $\varepsilon = 10^{-3}$~m, small compared
with the characteristic flow depth of the test cases. Reducing
$\varepsilon$ below $10^{-4}$~m did not change the computed profiles
within plotting accuracy.

The sediment flux $q_s$ is evaluated with the Meyer-Peter--M\"uller
formula, and the Exner equation is advanced explicitly with the same
time step, subject to the Courant restriction of the flow solver.

\section{Results}
The scheme is tested on a dam-break wave over a movable bed and on a
steady uniform flow perturbed by a migrating dune. For the dam-break
case the water front propagates over an initially dry reach, and the
regularised friction law prevents the singular behaviour that the
classical closure exhibits at the front.

The computed bed profiles agree with the reference solution on a
refined grid to within 2\% in the $L^1$ norm. The global conservation
error of the sediment volume remains below $10^{-6}$ for all runs,
independent of the mesh size.

The results are insensitive to the regularisation parameter: halving
$\varepsilon$ changes the maximum bed deformation by less than 0.5\%.
The tolerance $\epsilon$ of the Newton iteration was varied separately
and shows no influence on the converged solution.
